critical_code_review_comments: schedules.py: _send_telegram builds a Markdown-v1 message with the escape function `_escape_md` but the header uses NOTE 'NOCTUA\.osint' with escaped dot (that is MarkdownV2 syntax). Telegram parse_mode='Markdown' (legacy) does NOT accept `\.` — it will send the literal backslash. Recommend either switch parse_mode to 'MarkdownV2' (then escape must include -, ., !, (), etc.) OR remove the backslash before the dot. Not user-visible for the current tests (falls back to plain send if parse fails).

server.py public_takeover_check: uses `logger.exception(...)` inside except but `logger` is defined later in the file (line 841) after the function. If insert fails at cold start before logging is set up, this raises NameError. Move `logger` definition above the endpoint or replace with `logging.getLogger(__name__)` at the top.

server.py: two module-level dicts (_stats_cache and _public_rate_bucket) are NOT process-safe. Under gunicorn/uvicorn workers > 1 the cache is per-worker and the rate limit becomes 5*N per hour. Acceptable for MVP; for production move to Redis.

server.py public_stats: `total_scans = db.scans.estimated_document_count() + db.public_scans.estimated_document_count()` sums BOTH collections. If the intent is 'historical scans' that's OK, but the field name overlaps semantically with scans_this_month. Consider clarifying label on the landing page (currently 'Escaneos históricos' which is fine).

schedules.py set_telegram: allows saving token without hitting Telegram getMe (by design per spec). Consider adding an optional query flag ?validate=true that triggers a lightweight getMe call so a UI 'Save & verify' path exists without dual-writing.

Landing.jsx: `axios.get(`${API}/public/stats`)` on mount has no `withCredentials` (correct for public), but if the auth interceptor adds a Bearer token, it could leak. Not an issue today because auth uses cookies + explicit header setup, but worth an isolated axios instance for /public/* endpoints.

Settings.jsx: telegram Chat ID input uses `type='text'` and is disabled for FREE users (`disabled={!isPro}`) but the Bot Token KeyInput component does NOT have a disabled prop applied. Behavior is: FREE user can TYPE into token but Save/Test are disabled. Minor UX inconsistency vs Slack input (which is fully disabled). Consider disabling the token KeyInput for Free users too.
action_items: (Minor UX) Disable the Bot Token KeyInput for FREE users in Settings.jsx to match Slack input behavior (currently token field is typable but save/test are disabled).

(Minor) Fix `logger` reference ordering in server.py — public_takeover_check's exception handler references `logger` before it is defined at the bottom of the file. Move the `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` above module-level route definitions.
(Optional) Telegram Markdown escaping: header uses `NOCTUA\.osint` (MarkdownV2 style) with parse_mode='Markdown' — either drop the backslash or switch to parse_mode='MarkdownV2' consistently.
(Optional) Move _stats_cache and _public_rate_bucket to Redis for multi-worker production.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_telegram_public.py (new — 17 pytest cases covering Telegram + public endpoints)
test_credentials: Test sessions minted directly in MongoDB per /app/memory/test_credentials.md. UI test tokens (sess_ui_pro_/sess_ui_free_) were cleaned up after the run.
seed_data_creation: conftest.py free_user / pro_user fixtures used for backend pytest; additional ad-hoc Pro/Free tokens created & deleted for the UI Playwright run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both new features are green. Public rate-limit shares state across backend tests and manual UI runs (all one bucket per IP). If retesting the successful public scan flow from the same egress IP, restart backend to clear _public_rate_bucket. Telegram /test with real credentials would require live BotFather bot; fake tokens intentionally return ok:false with Telegram's 'Not Found'/'Unauthorized' description — this is expected behavior, not a bug. The one warning-not-failure surfaced during UI testing was that the JSX for the 'Guardado · <mask>' badge only appears when tgTokenSet && !tgToken; after save the tgToken state is cleared so it displays correctly (verified by screenshot).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs blocking either feature. All 17 new backend tests pass. All 10 UI flows pass. Minor code-review items are noted under critical_code_review_comments and action_items.
